name: Post-tropical Rachel
type: Remnant storm, swell and coastal flooding
headline: Rachel's remnants killed five members of one family in Ensenada and sent a long-period swell onto Southern California beaches already sitting 1–2 ft above the tide tables.
numbers: 5 in Ensenada (one family) + 1 Guerrero, Simon and Rachel combined
timeline: Major hurricane off southwestern Mexico, peak 105 kt.
Moves north over 28–29 °C water off Baja, staying tropical unusually far north.
Remnants cross northern Baja into the US Southwest; flash floods in Ensenada; long-period south swell hits south-facing beaches; new-moon spring tides.
Five victims from the same family recovered in Ensenada.

sections.The setup: Water off Baja California at 28–29 °C, several degrees above normal under El Niño and the marine heatwave, let Rachel keep its strength much farther north than usual.
sections.What amplified it: Sea level already 1–2 ft above predictions from the Kelvin wave and marine heatwave; new-moon spring tides on 10 October; the third big surf event in five weeks after Marie and Polo.
sections.How it ended: Cooler water and land interaction north of 30°N; the remnant low crossed into the Southwest.

sources.title: Latin Times: three storms, one coast
